chapter_title: CHANGES AROUND US PHYSICAL AND CHEMICAL

items.title: Identify Physical and Chemical Changes
items.explanation: Physical changes occur when a substance's appearance, size, shape, or state changes but no new substance is formed. Examples include melting ice cubes (solid to liquid), cutting paper, folding paper, drying clothes, and crushing chalk into powder. Chemical changes result in the formation of one or more new substances with different properties. Examples include burning wood, making popcorn from corn, adding beetroot extract to water, and mixing vinegar with baking soda to form carbon dioxide gas.
